chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
"The water of the well is ample; nothing corrupts it unless it changes."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The correct way to understand this report is that nothing corrupts it in such a way that it is not permissible to benefit from any of it except after drawing out all of it, unless it changes. But if it has not changed, then a certain amount is drawn from it, and benefit is taken from the remainder, as we have explained.

key_terms.لَا يُفْسِدُهُ: does not spoil or render it unusable
key_terms.نَزْحِ: drawing out water from a well
key_terms.وَاسِعٌ: abundant or extensive in a legal sense
key_terms.يَتَغَيَّرَ: to undergo change in its qualities
key_terms.يُنْتَفَعُ: it may be used or benefited from

ai.seo_question: Does impurity make well water unusable in Islamic law if the water does not change?
ai.summary: This hadith states that well water is not rendered unusable by mere contact with impurity unless its properties change. The accompanying explanation clarifies a legal ruling: if no change occurs, only a prescribed amount is removed and the rest remains usable.
